findings.title: Embedded-post author link inverts lightness percentages
findings.body: `.topic-meta-data h5 a` previously used `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%)`. This change passes `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%)` as the light-theme color and `scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 30%)` as the dark-theme color. Everywhere else in this PR the first `dark-light-choose` argument keeps the original lightness and the `$secondary` argument uses the complement (here that would be 30% / 70%). Light themes therefore render this link much lighter than before, and dark themes get a darker gray than the muted color this rule is meant to produce, so the embedded-post author name loses contrast on a dark background.

findings.title: Group member name color collapsed to the title color
findings.body: `.user-stream .group-member-info .name` was `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%)`, distinct from the adjacent `.title` at 50%. The replacement uses `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 50%))`, the same pair as `.title`. Light-theme names become lighter than before, and names and titles are no longer visually distinct in either theme. The dark branch should be `scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 70%)` with the original 30% primary color kept for light themes.

findings.title: Mobile group member name uses the title's 50% scale
findings.body: Mobile `.group-member-info .name` was `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%)` while `.title` was 50%. Both are now `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 50%))`. That lightens the name on light themes and removes the name/title contrast on light and dark themes. It should keep 30% of `$primary` for light and use 70% of `$secondary` for dark, matching the transform applied to other 30% primary colors.

findings.title: Mobile topic-map heading lightness changed from 20% to 50%
findings.body: `.topic-map h3` was `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 20%)`. It is now `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 50%))`, which is the h4 color copied onto the heading. The desktop rule for the same heading correctly keeps 20% of `$primary` and uses 80% of `$secondary`. On mobile, light-theme topic-map headings become lighter than before, and dark-theme headings do not match the desktop complement, so the heading is no longer darker/stronger than the h4 beneath it.

findings.title: Mobile custom-message-length swaps the light and dark scales
findings.body: `.custom-message-length` was `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%)`. The new value is `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 70%))`. The desktop stylesheet for the same selector correctly keeps 70% of `$primary` and uses 30% of `$secondary`. On mobile the light-theme hint becomes much darker than the existing design, and the dark-theme color is the complement of 30% rather than of 70%, so it will not match desktop or the rest of this change.

findings.title: Category badge notification color still scales $primary only
findings.body: In the same file whose topic-list header, cell, excerpt, and education colors were wrapped in `dark-light-choose`, `.topic-list.categories .category .badge-notification` still sets `color: scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%)`. On a dark theme `$primary` is already near white, so raising its lightness makes this transparent-background notification text nearly the same as primary text instead of the muted gray used by the neighboring list colors. It should follow the same 50% `$primary` / 50% `$secondary` pair used for the other 50% text colors in this file.
